html:
The leader of the People's Republic of China since 2012, when he became general secretary of the Chinese Communist Party. He became president in 2013.

He is the son of Xi Zhongxun, a revolutionary veteran who was purged under Mao. During the Cultural Revolution the young Xi was sent to a poor village in Shaanxi, as part of the Down to the Countryside movement. He then rose through provincial posts in Hebei, Fujian, Zhejiang and Shanghai.

As leader he has:

  • run a wide anti-corruption campaign that also removed rivals;
  • launched the Belt and Road Initiative in 2013, to build ports, railways and roads abroad;
  • tightened control over the press, the internet, Xinjiang and Hong Kong;
  • had the limit of two terms on the presidency removed in 2018.

He has gathered more personal power than any Chinese leader since Mao, ending the shared leadership that Deng Xiaoping had set up.
sum: The leader of the People's Republic of China since 2012, when he became general secretary of the Chinese Communist Party. He became president in 2013.
